snapshot_note: v0.53.0 released on develop 2026-07-26 - `-static-libmadc` now works in the .o LINK lane, lifting forest-carriers S5's last stated boundary. The AOT ledger is carried as MIR modules, so the pieces a program needs are pulled into a PRIVATE object-mode context, generated, emitted with MIR_gen_object_emit, and merged into the same builder as the .o inputs. Through the merge deliberately: a builder's symbol table is append-only (MIR_object_add_symbol never dedupes by name), and the unification that turns the inputs' UNDEF entries into references to the runtime's definitions IS the merge - so the runtime rides the ONE unification implementation, on the read-back path both containers (ELF ET_REL and MH_OBJECT) already gate. No new format code, no fork change. Generalized rather than duplicated: cir_ledger_pull takes a SEED list (the builder's UNDEF names join the module imports under the same not-defined filter), and the cover analysis takes the reference LIST rather than its source (source lanes pass context imports, the .o lane passes MIR_object_undef_name) - same classifier, same two diagnostics. Fixed on the way: the AOT-ledger carrier now opens HEADER-ONLY (the ledger is a container-global segment, but the probe ran complete_open, which binds the frozen string pool and arena into LIVE parse state - it died with 'forest thaw requires a live string pool' in a lane with no lexer). New -fno-eval-shims: every .o carries __madc_shim_* host-call adapters whose twelve madc_value_* imports are Tier B, an executable emit from source skips them and a .o cannot know, so the build says it (the -fPIC shape). Fork unchanged (1.0-madc.0.52.0 @ba216dea).

live_handoff: *** SESSION 2026-07-27 #17 — READ THIS FIRST. THE NEXT TASK IS FIXED AND NON-NEGOTIABLE: docs/plans/2026-07-27-angle-bracket-consolidation.md. Do that BEFORE resuming the libc++ track or anything else. WHY IT IS FIRST: a `<` used as a LESS-THAN OPERATOR inside a template argument list is misparsed as opening a nested template-argument list, so the scanner eats an operator `>` as its closer and runs to EOF. THE ROOT CAUSE IS DUPLICATION, and the owner called it before I measured it: `grep -n "++angle_depth" src/parser.cpp` returns SIX sites and exactly ONE is guarded. History: 2026-06-05 (e7b06f30) writes three unguarded scanners; 2026-06-07 (2e853dee) finds the bug and fixes it IN ONE PLACE with a comment naming this exact shape and symptom; 2026-06-09 (c9fd2227) adds ANOTHER unguarded scanner TWO DAYS AFTER the fix. Site 3379 is the sharpest case — it computes paren_depth and simply never consults it on the `<`. So the correct rule has existed for seven weeks and five siblings never learned it: the Rule #4 failure mode exactly. DO NOT fix this by adding the guard five more times — that is the move that produced the current state. Extract ONE tracker, migrate every site onto it, let -Wunused confirm each cut, and add scripts/check-one-angle-tracker.sh to fulltest so a seventh copy cannot be written (precedent: check-no-std-hardcoding.sh). The plan doc has the slices, the per-slice gates, and the behaviour-preserving cautions (the sites differ in how they USE the depths — unify the update rule, not the use). *** SESSION 2026-07-27 #16: P2.0 `-stdlib=` SHIPPED — a C++ standard library is now a selectable FLAVOR, and selecting one REPLACES the include search list. Branch feature/libcxx-flavor-claude @e114cbae, NOT merged, NOT released. Read this, then docs/plans/2026-07-26-libcxx-flavor-plan.md (its "Worklist status" table is the actionable list). === 1. WHAT LANDED @e114cbae. A search list is a property of the standard library, not an ordering preference, so gen_sys_includes.sh now emits ONE TABLE PER FLAVOR — madc_stdlib_flavors[] of { name, paths, compiler_owned_dir } in the generated src/sys_include_paths.cpp — and -stdlib= picks between them. That is what clang's driver does: one list built per library, not one list reordered. The resource dir is per-flavor too, because gcc's and clang's differ and it is the slot madc's embedded freestanding set occupies in the search order. THE MOTIVATING FAILURE, now a passing gate leg: std::string under libc++ died in /usr/include/c++/13/stdlib.h on `using std::abort;`, because libc++'s <cstdlib> reaches the C library through `#include_next <stdlib.h>` and, with the GNU C++ dirs still on the path behind libc++, that walk lands on GNU's wrapper. -I can put a library FIRST; first is not the same as ONLY. === 2. THREE PROPERTIES OF THE DESIGN, keep them. (a) WHICH FLAVORS EXIST IS A BUILD-HOST FACT, DISCOVERED, NEVER LISTED. The default is whatever $(CXX) resolves to; an alternate is recorded when a probe reports a DIFFERENT library. The candidate probe commands ($(CXX) -stdlib=..., clang++-18 -stdlib=libc++, ...) are tool SPELLINGS, not answers — each is asked what it actually resolved to by reading the library's own _LIBCPP_VERSION / __GLIBCXX__, so a candidate whose compiler or library is absent reports nothing and drops out. The `!= default` test is what makes a silent fallback impossible to mistake for a second flavor. MADC_STDLIB_ALT_CXX overrides discovery. (b) ONE READER. All five consumers — the lexer's <...> resolution, is_system_header_path, #include_next, and the two embedded-header partition predicates — now go through Program::sys_include_paths() / compiler_owned_include_dir(), which also collapsed three copies of the no-compiler fallback list into one. Deleting the old globals let the compiler confirm the sweep was complete. Two of those sites previously skipped the fallback entirely; centralizing gives it to them, which only changes behaviour on a host with no compiler to probe, and in the correct direction. (c) AN UNAVAILABLE FLAVOR FAILS LOUD, naming what THIS BINARY was built with — because availability is a property of the machine that built it, a diagnostic listing the flag's possible spellings would be useless. Bare `-stdlib=` is rejected too (it must not match an unnamed entry on a compiler-less build host). === 3. REACHABLE FROM ALL THREE SURFACES a flavor can arrive on: -stdlib= on the CLI; `stdlib =` in madc.ini (CLI wins, same precedence as `std`); and -stdlib= in a compile_commands.json entry — that last one because a libc++ project's manifest carries it and IGNORING IT WOULD SILENTLY COMPILE AGAINST THE WRONG LIBRARY'S HEADERS. === 4. THE NEXT BLOCKER, with a two-line reducer and six hypotheses already ELIMINATED. std::string under -stdlib=libc++ now reaches deep into libc++ and stops at c++/v1/cctype:111, `using ::isalnum;`. Reducer: `#include <string_view>` then `#include <cwchar>`. ELIMINATED BY MEASUREMENT (do not re-test): include resolution/#include_next (the -v trace shows the exact clang chain cctype -> c++/v1/ctype.h -> /usr/include/ctype.h, so glibc's header IS read); PCH divergence (zero `precompiled` hits in that trace); inline namespaces (`namespace std { inline namespace __1 { using ::isalnum; } }` compiles); #undef dropping the function (`#define isalnum(c) 0` then `#undef isalnum` then `using ::isalnum;` compiles); <string_view> poisoning global lookup (<string_view>+<ctype.h>+using compiles, and so does <string_view>+<cctype>); and every header alone (<cctype>, <cwctype>, <__string/char_traits.h>, <string_view>, <stdexcept> all compile). So it needs <cwchar> SPECIFICALLY plus a prior header — <cwchar> alone gets PAST cctype and fails later at its own cwchar:202, a `std::wcslen` CALL, a different construct with a different diagnostic. And note <string_view> already pulls <cwchar> transitively, so the explicit second include should be a guard-skip no-op yet changes the outcome. THAT is the thread: parse/registration state, not which file was opened. === 5. A PROBE TRAP THAT COST ME AN HOUR, recorded because it will recur. `isalnum(65)` COMPILES UNDER MADC WHETHER OR NOT isalnum IS DECLARED — the implicit-function/dlsym fallback accepts it. An early probe used exactly that and I concluded "the ctype chain works standalone", which was not what the probe measured. PROBE A DECLARATION WITH `using ::X;`, NEVER WITH A CALL. This is the same class as the `(int)std::is_same<>::value` cast trap from session #15: suspect the probe before theorizing about the subject. === 6. EVIDENCE. Full battery at the pre-final build: JIT 760 passed / 0 failed / 0 timed out / 9 skipped; EXE 744/0; OBJ 744/0. fulltest's only failure was scripts/forest_config_gate.sh asserting the schema's accepted-key list literally — adding the madc.ini `stdlib` key moved it. Both tests that pin that list (tests/unit/test_config_file.cpp and the gate) were updated; the duplication is deliberate, they pin one contract at two layers, and loosening either to make a schema change cheaper is the wrong trade. After the two post-battery source edits (the bare-`-stdlib=` guard and the empty-flavor-list diagnostic) I rebuilt and re-ran ONLY what those edits can reach: forest_config_gate OK, libcxx_gate OK on all 10 legs, test_config_file 19/19 cases 88/88 assertions, plus manual checks that bare `-stdlib=` is rejected with the flavor list and that `stdlib = libc++` in madc.ini works end-to-end. Those two edits live in functions no test reaches without passing -stdlib=, which is the named boundary for not re-running the battery. === 7. NEXT, in priority order. (a) The cctype blocker in §4 — the reducer is two lines, start from the guard-skip observation. (b) is_destructible evaluates wrong, which is what makes is_trivially_destructible wrong; madc's own __has_trivial_destructor is CORRECT (1/0/1 matching g++), so the defect is upstream in the SFINAE/declval chain — the real tsubst burn-down. (c) &S::n still reports "Unknown namespace 'S'" (parseAddressOfExpression, a different function from the one fixed @3167da3c). === 8. A CONFLATION FOUND AND DELIBERATELY LEFT ALONE. cir_native_link_env() in src/madc_cir.cpp picks the C++ runtime for DT_NEEDED — libc++ vs libstdc++.so.6 — behind a host `#ifdef __APPLE__`. That is the platform-means-library conflation this whole track exists to undo, and it is doubly confused: the #ifdef is a property of the machine madc was BUILT on while DT_NEEDED describes the TARGET. It works today only because the two happen to agree. It belongs to the P2.3 flavor switch; written up in the plan doc's P2.3 section rather than fixed here, because the native link lane is a different surface than P2.0's. === 9. STATE. develop @9af72c00 = v0.53.0, master @277dc086 = v0.48.0, fork @ba216dea = 1.0-madc.0.52.0 UNCHANGED — still no fork change needed; everything remains Tier-1 madc-side. Feature branch pushed, working tree clean. The generated src/sys_include_paths.cpp is gitignored as before and now carries both flavor tables; a build host without clang/libc++ simply records one flavor and -stdlib=libc++ errors there, by design. === 10. ADDENDUM (same session, @87427778): A SYSTEM HEADER IS SYSTEM CODE IN EITHER PATH SPELLING. libc++'s stddef.h is DELIBERATELY re-includable — a first visit through its `#if defined(__need_size_t)` branch does NOT define _LIBCPP_STDDEF_H, so a later full visit must re-enter. That only happens under gcc's guard-checked multiple-include semantics, which should_tokenize_include() applies to SYSTEM headers; a header read as USER code gets madc's require-once rule and its second visit is dropped FOREVER, after which <cstddef> #errors and says exactly why. EVERY libc++ header was being read as user code: should_tokenize_include() canonicalizes the file through realpath while is_system_header_path() prefix-matched the RAW generated table entry, and clang reports its own search dir as /usr/lib/llvm-18/bin/../include/c++/v1 — the spellings never match. GNU's paths are already canonical, which is why this waited for libc++. FIX: the classifier also matches realpath'd prefixes, cached per flavor; unresolvable entries keep their raw spelling so cross/hosted tables naming an absent sysroot still work; the raw compare stays first so nothing that worked changes. PROVEN BEFORE IT WAS WRITTEN via a build with MADC_SYS_INCLUDE_PREFIX_MAP rewriting the path to canonical form. Gate leg 11 keys on libc++'s own #error text so a regression names its own cause. REACH BEYOND libc++: is_system_header_path() also gates CIR inline-body emission (reachability DCE), so libc++ headers were on the wrong side of that decision too. TWO CORRECTIONS TO MY OWN WORK, both of which changed conclusions: (i) my bisect harness classified compiles by `head -1` of the output, and madc prints a BLANK LINE before every diagnostic, so EVERY FAILURE READ AS A PASS — five headers recorded as compiling actually failed and the wrong table reached a committed plan doc; re-measuring on EXIT STATUS showed five DISTINCT failures and led to the root cause within the hour. (ii) HOSTTAB_GEN regenerates the include table at Makefile PARSE time, so an ordinary `make` silently overwrote a hand-generated table and my first canonicalization experiment never ran — without catching that I would have concluded the fix was wrong from a test that did not happen. Pass the env through make. STILL OPEN: cctype:111 `using ::isalnum;` from <string_view> SURVIVES this fix and is a DIFFERENT bug. Reducer is ONE line. Six hypotheses eliminated (see the plan doc); live thread = <cctype> compiles alone and inside <cwchar> but not inside <string_view>, so ask what registration state ~290 preceding headers leave behind. Battery after the fix: 760/0/0/9 JIT, 744/0 EXE, 744/0 OBJ, libcxx_gate 11/11. === 11. ADDENDUM (@cf8f035c): &S::n FIXED — worklist item (c) closed. parseAddressOfExpression's tkNS block consulted only namespace_map, so a CLASS qualifier could never resolve and reported "Unknown namespace 'S'" — a diagnostic naming the wrong thing. Address-side twin of @3167da3c (which added the class arm to parsePostfixChain for the VALUE side); both arms now converge on the same tail that sets vfADDRTAKEN and builds the TokenAddrOf, so the namespace path changed only in indentation. DELIBERATELY NOT routed through resolve_class_static_member_value(): that helper prefers a folded in-class constant and a CONSTANT HAS NO ADDRESS, so the address path asks for the STORAGE the out-of-class definition created (class_static_member_storage_name() — parseDeclaration folds C::m to C__m, now written once for the two callers that need different answers about the same name). A declared-but-never-defined member gets its own diagnostic instead of a pointer to nothing; a class qualifier with a non-static-data member gets another. Test teststaticmemberaddr.mad checks PROPERTIES not just compilation — writes through the pointer visible through the qualified name and vice versa, address stable across expressions, survives a mutating call, a double member yields double* (pointer type from the member, not a fallback), two classes' members distinct, namespace form still works — and matches g++ AND clang++ byte-for-byte. BASELINE MOVED: 761/0/0/9 JIT, 745/0 EXE, 745/0 OBJ (+1 each = this test). REMAINING WORKLIST: (a-residue) cctype:111 using ::isalnum from <string_view>, one-line reducer, six hypotheses eliminated — see the plan doc; (b) is_destructible/declval SFINAE chain, the real tsubst burn-down. === 12. ADDENDUM — cctype:111 ROOT CAUSE FOUND (fix NOT written; this is the top NEXT item). It is NOT a libc++ problem and NOT an include problem: it is a C++ PARSER bug, reducible to EIGHT LINES with no library headers. `template <class T, class U> struct cmp<T, U, typename vt<decltype(declval<T>() < declval<U>())>::type> {};` — madc says 'Unexpected end of data', g++ and clang print `1 0`. The `<` in `declval<T>() < declval<U>()` is a LESS-THAN OPERATOR, but the scanner reading the partial specialization's template-argument list treats it as opening a nested argument list, consumes declval<U>'s `>` as the closer, and runs to EOF. THE CASCADE, and it is worth understanding before touching anything: libc++'s __utility/is_pointer_in_range.h contains exactly that construct. It dies mid-header, so its _LIBCPP_BEGIN_NAMESPACE_STD never opens a namespace — and the matching _LIBCPP_END_NAMESPACE_STD then CLOSES SCOPES THAT WERE NEVER OPENED. From there the scope stack is wrong, later global declarations (glibc's isalnum among them) are unreachable from ::, and `using ::isalnum;` fails at cctype:111 SIX HEADERS DOWNSTREAM of the actual defect. Every order-dependence in my earlier bisects was just which header first drags in is_pointer_in_range.h. THE CORRECT RULE IS ALREADY IMPLEMENTED, IN ONE PLACE: parser.cpp:38774 tracks angle brackets ONLY outside parens/subscripts, and its comment cites this exact shape (decltype(forward<_Tp>(t) < forward<_Up>(u))) together with the same consumed-to-EOF symptom. A SIBLING scanner lacks the guard. There are SIX angle_depth scanners (parser.cpp:3320 collect_template_argument_spelling [has paren_depth], 18083/18104 spelling helpers, 38358 collect_template_default_argument, 38716 [the fixed reference], 45465 skip_template_suffix_tokens, 48445). SIX COPIES OF ONE RULE IS THE REAL FINDING — the fix is to make them SHARE it, not to add the guard a seventh time (design-principles.md, no-parallel-implementations.md). QUEUED BEHIND IT, seen once is_pointer_in_range.h is worked around: <compare> -> math.h:414 'Unknown namespace std::__math' — a NESTED namespace qualifier, the same family as the &S::n fix but for a qualified name. NOTE the fix was deliberately NOT started: angle-bracket disambiguation is delicate, and there was not enough remaining budget to gate a change in that area (the battery is ~40 min).

VLA NOT DEALLOCATED ON BACKWARD GOTO: a `goto` jumping back to before a VLA's declaration must deallocate the VLA (gcc/C semantics; gcc-torture 20040811-1.c). madc lowers VLAs as malloc + __attribute__((cleanup)), which frees only on SCOPE EXIT, not on the backward goto re-entering the scope — so a backward-goto loop over a VLA LEAKS one allocation per iteration. 20040811-1.c leaks ~2GB over 1e6 iterations; it passes only when memory is available (it OOM-SIGSEGV'd when the MIR fork's 128MB code-holder reservation reduced headroom — see mir_fork; arch-gated off x86-64, so it passes again). Proper fix: free the VLA at the backward goto. Separate future slice.
